answer: To mitigate Sybil incursions within autonomous agent clusters, networks mandate a cryptographic ember of staked collateral. This creates a value-at-risk barrier where deploying a sable swarm of fake nodes requires massive capital. Furthermore, verifying a hardware-bound relic, such as a Trusted Execution Environment certificate, anchors each identity to physical silicon, ensuring that duplicating a persona costs the attacker the full market price of secure hardware.
